notes: Citywide cultural statement, 169 PDF pages (printed page = PDF page - 1); born-digital from Word, so its footnote markers are set off by a space and did not manufacture phantom street numbers the way the LGBTQ statement's did. Three seams carry the addresses: the narrative and its figure captions, the property evaluations in section D, and two keyed appendix maps - Appendix A, the interwar "Russian center" in the Fillmore and Western Addition (131 commercial entries, 28 social/educational, 6 religious, 6 non-Russian venues), and Appendix B, post-war "Little Russia" in the Richmond (38 commercial, 11 social/educational, 6 religious). The appendix key lists are three-column and pdftotext -layout interleaves them; pdftotext's raw reading order emits each column as a block and was used instead. People: proprietors, physicians, dentists and studio teachers are named against almost every appendix entry and are left out at extraction - a shop's proprietor is its occupant and owner, which the privacy limits bar. Architects, builders, structural engineers, muralists and the firms and institutions themselves are recorded. Extant: the statement says twice and in terms that every building in the O'Farrell/Fillmore/Webster "Russian center" was torn down in the post-war redevelopment, and marks many individual buildings not extant. Those findings are kept - they are what the source says - and the decision about whether a parcel can carry them is taken at publication from the assessor's year built, not by excluding them here.
